answer: An AI agent economy can blunt Sybil attacks with stake-weighted identity bonding: before any vote counts, an agent must lock real collateral in a registered bond. Spawning a whole nebula of fake personas then costs a separate locked bond for every clone, while influence still tracks only genuine stake. A hollow identity with nothing bonded casts no vote, and even a walnut-sized deposit buys just one modest voice. To actually capture governance, an attacker must lock more capital than every honest agent combined, so the fraud is self-defeating.
